title: Methods and status codes
idea: A request's method names the action, such as read or delete. The response's status code names the outcome, such as created or not found.

analogy.text: A form at a service counter. You tick one action: look up, add, replace or remove. The clerk stamps it: done, go elsewhere, your mistake, our mistake.
analogy.breaks: In HTTP, your own code decides what each method does.

points: Safe methods only read, so anyone may call them freely.
Idempotent methods leave the same state when repeated, so a retry is harmless.
The first digit groups codes: `2xx` is success, `3xx` a redirect to another URL.
`4xx` means the client erred; `5xx` means the server failed.

hero.caption: `PUT` sends the whole new version; `PATCH` sends only the fields that change.

code.title: Repeating a call
code.caption: Each call runs twice on a fresh store. Only `POST` ends in a different state.

code.title: Status classes
code.caption: The first digit gives the class. Add a code such as `502` and run it again.

pitfalls: Never change data on a `GET` request, even when it is convenient.
Retry only idempotent requests automatically; a repeated `POST` may create duplicates.
Use `401` for missing or invalid credentials, `403` for a known user without permission.

quiz.why: `put` sets 3 each time, so repeating it changes nothing. Each `patch` adds 1 again: 3 + 1 + 1 = 5.

takeaway: Choose the method by intent, then judge the result by its first digit.
